newsitem.title: UK: Russia slips in emerging debt market.
newsitem.headline: Russia slips in emerging debt market.

text.p: Russia dropped on Monday in an emerging debt market that is getting rattled by worries over the outlook for U.S. interest rates and taking the opportunity to cash in some profits, traders said.
In morning trading, there was little activity and most prices held around the lower levels they touched at the end of last week where they had been dragged by sagging U.S. Treasuries and stocks.
"Russia opened unchanged. It's now down about half a point on some agressive street selling," a U.S. bank trader said.
The latest news out of Moscow has President Boris Yeltsin continung to recover from pneumonia at a state residence outside the capital.
However, he had no meetings scheduled for Monday and no new footage of him has been shown on television for three weeks, even longer than the period after his heart operation in November.
Fresh demonstrations in Bulgaria at the weekend had no significant impact on prices, though the lev hit new lows this morning.
Talks between the ruling Socialist party and the opposition, which is demanding an early general election, remain deadlocked.
Traders are now watching to make sure that Bulgaria does meet its Brady coupon payment as promised.
The market is also watching progress in attempts in Brazil to change the constitution to allow Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for another term as president.
According to local newspapers, the government is increasingly confident that it will be able to make the amendments.
Traders said the market will also be watching for a fresh bunch of U.S. data, including the first fourth quarter GDP growth estimates.
